title: GSA and OpenAI sign 27-month OneGov ChatGPT deal at $0 license fee
subtitle: The new agreement zeroes out per-seat pricing for federal, state, local, and tribal government users and cuts usage costs in half through 2028.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: The U.S. General Services Administration announced a new OneGov agreement with OpenAI on September 15, 2026, replacing the expiring $1-per-agency ChatGPT Enterprise deal that had covered about 3.5 million federal workers. The successor runs 27 months — October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2028 — and drops the standard $15 per user per month license to $0 with no minimum commitment. Eligible usage across the OpenAI API and ChatGPT Business tiers is discounted 50 percent, and eligibility widens beyond federal agencies to state, local, and tribal governments.

The structural change is the shift from a fixed nominal license to a consumption-based contract with the license fee removed entirely. Under the old $1 arrangement the price signal was 'take it,' but usage was uncapped and hard to attribute; the OneGov 2.0 terms invert that — the seat is free, and metered usage carries the real cost, discounted but visible. GSA estimates eligibility now reaches roughly 23 million people across the three levels of government.

The deal lands in a season when Washington has been pushing consumption-based OneGov templates across cloud, security, and AI vendors, and while OpenAI itself has publicly stepped back from a 2026 IPO on stated safety grounds. Federal AI procurement in 2026 has moved from pilot budgets to line-item spend, and locking a 27-month floor at half-off is the kind of anchor that shapes downstream contracts with Microsoft, Anthropic, Google, and any others chasing the same buyer.

Takeaway for learners: pay attention to how the pricing is structured, not just the sticker. A free license paired with per-token usage moves the cost from procurement into operations — the same lesson private-sector AI buyers learned in 2024. If your school or employer is evaluating an AI tool, model what a real month of use costs before celebrating a headline 'free' tier.
